newsitem.title: UK: UK will stick to current economic policies - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK will stick to current economic policies - Clarke.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday he would stick to economic policies to safeguard the recovery.

"The British economy will enter the New Year in the best shape for a generation. I will stick to policies that will enable us to keep it up and go on to make our recovered prosperity more safe and secure for years to come," he said in a pre-Christmas statement.

He welcomed Friday's GDP and current account figures which showed GDP grew 0.7 percent in the third quarter and a trade deficit of 71 million stg versus a surplus of 344 million stg in the second quarter.
"Today's figures show living standards up 4.5 percent on a year ago and, in the last half year, Britain's best trading performance for a decade," Clarke said.

"This week we have had a string of news showing that British hard work and enterprise are bringing rewards. Rising living standards, falling unemployment, low inflation, buoyant retail sales and an excellent trading performance," Clarke added.
Earlier this week, data showed unemployment fell by a record 95,800 in November and retail sales grew by 0.7 percent.
